title: fix(plugin-detail): `record:activity` refuses a non-integer row cap instead of flooring it
body:
Fixes #10096

`Clause-②: no` — this PULLS BACK to the declared contract (`z.number().int().positive()`). It relaxes no accept set and widens no public surface.

## What changed

`normalizeLimit` in `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/recordActivityFeed.ts` now REFUSES a non-integer row cap to `DEFAULT_ACTIVITY_LIMIT` instead of flooring it:

```diff
-  const n = Math.floor(Number(value));
-  return Number.isFinite(n) && n > 0 ? n : DEFAULT_ACTIVITY_LIMIT;
+  const n = Number(value);
+  return Number.isInteger(n) && n > 0 ? n : DEFAULT_ACTIVITY_LIMIT;
```

`Number.isInteger` replaces `Number.isFinite` and nothing else. That is the shape `normalizeHistoryLimit` landed for the sibling `record:history` in objectui#10093.

Also reached, deliberately: `record:chatter` / `record:discussion` resolve `feed.limit` through this same function, and `RecordChatterProps.feed` **is** `RecordActivityProps` — the same declared member, so the same refusal.

## The premise, re-taken first-hand before any edit

| leg | how it was settled | reading |
|---|---|---|
| the defect is live | the shipped bytes of `normalizeLimit` extracted from the file and EXECUTED, with the file's blob hash printed in the same command and equal to its `HEAD` blob | `normalizeLimit(2.5)` answered **2** |
| the contract refuses it | `RecordActivityProps.safeParse({ limit: 2.5 })` executed against the resolved `@objectstack/spec`; source re-read on objectstack `origin/main` | `invalid_type` — "expected int, received number". The declaration is `limit: z.number().int().positive().default(20)`, so the spec's own default agrees with `DEFAULT_ACTIVITY_LIMIT` |
| the pinned set cannot discriminate | the four existing cases run against BOTH the current and the repaired function in one command | `0`, `-3`, `undefined`, `'lots'` → `20` on both. They cannot fail in either direction |

A fourth reading, worth stating because the card calls objectui#10093 landed: it is **not** landed at the time of this run — still open, not merged, `record-history.tsx` on `origin/main` carries no `normalizeHistoryLimit`. The precedent was therefore read from that pull request's diff rather than from the tree. `origin/main` was re-fetched immediately before the final gate run; it had moved by one unrelated console i18n commit that touches no file in `packages/plugin-detail`, so nothing was merged in.

## The card's THIRD site: SETTLED as an internal clamp, not repaired

The third site is `applyFeedConfig`'s `const size = Math.max(1, Math.floor(pageSize) || DEFAULT_ACTIVITY_LIMIT);` — the same `Math.max(1, …)` expression objectui#10093 removed from the sibling. **It is not the same defect, and it is left unchanged.** The reading that makes it an internal clamp, measured rather than assumed:

- `pageSize` is not an authored member. It is the paging WINDOW.
- Both call sites compute it identically: `record-activity.tsx` and `record-chatter.tsx` each hold `const pageSize = limit * (extraPages + 1)`, where `limit` is already `normalizeLimit(...)`'s answer.
- `extraPages` is a `React.useState(0)` whose only writer, at both sites, is `setExtraPages((n) => n + 1)`.
- `applyFeedConfig` is exported from its module but **not** from the package barrel (`packages/plugin-detail/src/index.tsx` publishes `ACTIVITY_TYPE_TO_FEED_TYPE`, `UNMAPPED_ACTIVITY_FEED_TYPE`, `activityRowToFeedItem`, `resetUnknownActivityTypeWarnings` and the `SysActivityRow` type, and nothing else from it), so those two renderers are the whole production population.

⇒ a positive integer times a positive integer. `Math.floor` is the identity on it, the `||` arm never fires, and `Math.max(1, …)` never lifts: there is no refused authored value here for the clamp to repair. On the sibling it sat between an UNNORMALIZED authored member and the wire, which is exactly what made it a repair there.

That reading rests on `normalizeLimit` returning an INTEGER, so it is pinned rather than only written down. The reasoning is recorded at the site, and the test named "a refused cap widens the window to the default rather than narrowing it" ties the two sites together: it goes red if a fraction ever reaches that line again, because then the clamp's floor — not the resolver — would be deciding the window.

## The pin

New file: `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/__tests__/recordActivityFeed.rowLimitRefusal-10096.test.tsx`.

It reads the helper AND the wire, because a normalizer that refuses correctly is defeated by a floor or a `Math.max(1, …)` re-appearing downstream, and only the `$top` that reaches `DataSource.find()` sees both.

**RED before / GREEN after**, the subject file's blob hash printed in the same command as each run:

- RED, on blob `5ab2ef32b` (equal to its `HEAD` blob, working tree otherwise clean): `Tests 6 failed | 9 passed (15)`. The six that failed:
  - `refuses a fractional cap — ⛔ not a floor`
  - `refuses a fractional cap written as a numeric STRING, having read it`
  - `a fractional cap never becomes a fractional or floored $top` (received `3`, expected `21`)
  - `the properties read point answers identically`
  - `a refused cap widens the window to the default rather than narrowing it` (received a 2-row page, expected all 6)
  - `names nothing on the developer channel when it refuses`
- GREEN, on blob `2b9b44812`, with the repaired resolver echoed by the same command: `Test Files 2 passed (2) · Tests 76 passed (76)` over the new file plus the pre-existing `recordActivityFeed.test.ts`.

The nine that passed in the RED run are the controls, and they are the point: they include every one of the four values that were already pinned. Those four are annotated in place now, in `recordActivityFeed.test.ts`, so the next reader cannot mistake them for coverage of this.

## What this deliberately does NOT do

- **The default stays 20.** `record:history` defaults to 50; they differ on purpose and unifying them is a product decision reserved by objectui#10005's triage comment. The pin spells `20` literally rather than importing it, so it fails if the default moves.
- **Numeric-string coercion stays.** `normalizeLimit('5')` is still `5`, pinned as a control at the helper and at the wire. What narrows is the admitted value SET, not how a node's value is read. `normalizeLimit('2.5')` is refused for the value it reads to, not for being a string.
- **The refusal stays silent.** Whether this family should warn is objectui#10097, an open decision. The silence is pinned as a decision so whoever rules it changes this file deliberately.

This is a user-visible behaviour change, so it is a real `patch`, not an empty declaration.
- `pnpm changeset:check`, `pnpm check:changeset-claims`, `pnpm check:pending-changeset-literals`, `pnpm check:control-bytes`, `pnpm check:new-line-citations` — all exit 0 on the pushed commit. Two of their verdicts are worth quoting rather than summarising: control-bytes read `OK (scanned 8120 tracked text file(s); skipped 85 binary)`, and the line-citation gate read `0 new citation(s), enforcement report-only`. ⚠️ `check:changeset-claims` passed but printed `Read, but nothing to judge … ⛔ Not the same answer as a clean one` over this change's own changeset body — that is because the body cites by content and spells no line address for it to resolve, which is the intended shape, not a silent skip.

The narrowing is that other packages were not linted; the invariance that makes it a measurement rather than a skip is that this repo's flat config extends `tseslint.configs.recommended` and declares no `parserOptions.project` and no `projectService`, i.e. **type-aware linting is not enabled**, so nothing in this diff can move the verdict of a file it does not touch. The new pin file carries 3 `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` WARNINGS from its `as any` mock harness, the same shape the neighbouring pins use (986 of that warning in this package already); the repo-wide `pnpm lint` farm belongs to CI.

## Out of scope, noted and not filed

- `record-activity.tsx` also spells `Math.max(1, pageSize)` twice — at the `$top` it sends and at the `hasMore` comparison. Same reading as the settled clamp: `pageSize` is already a positive integer there, so both are the identity. Not a reproducible defect, outside this card's file surface, and not swept.
- `@objectstack/spec` refuses the numeric STRING `'5'` outright (`invalid_type: expected number, received string`) while this renderer family still resolves it to `5`. That is a live divergence between the contract and the renderer, but objectui#10093 kept the coercion deliberately and this card explicitly reserves it, so it is recorded here rather than changed or filed.
- The claim comment quotes this member as `z.number().int().positive().optional()`; the actual `RecordActivityProps.limit` declaration is `.default(20)`. `.optional()` is the sibling `RecordHistoryProps.limit`'s spelling. Nothing downstream turns on it — the refusal target is the same either way — but the quoted spelling is not this block's.
